title: fix(fields): give a read-only `file` field a per-file view/download link
body:
Fixes #9161

A `file` field in read-only state produced no way to reach the file it holds. On the
record-detail page a multi-value field rendered the bare text `1 file`, a single value
rendered a bare filename, and the edit-state row rendered a filename beside a delete
button — the reporter's DOM reading of the field block was one BUTTON element (the
delete icon) and ZERO anchors. Every other layer was proven healthy on the card: the
record read returns the expanded `{id, name, size, mimeType, url}`, the signing endpoint
answers 200, fetching the signed URL answers 200 with a correct `content-disposition`,
and a cross-owner read answers 200 too. So only the rendering was broken — and it was
broken on three surfaces at once.

## What changed

All three read faces now render, **per file**, its name AND a keyboard-reachable
view/download link.

- `FileCellRenderer` (`packages/fields/src/index.tsx`) — the renderer a record-detail
  page actually resolves for `file` — normalises through `readFileValues`, the treatment
  `ImageCellRenderer` already applies to the same spec family, so an expanded value, a
  string URL, a CDN link and an unexpanded bare `sys_file` id all resolve.
- `FileField`'s `readonly` branch and its edit-state file rows draw the same affordance
  (`packages/fields/src/widgets/FileField.tsx`).
- The anchor itself lives once, in a new internal module
  `packages/fields/src/widgets/file-affordance.tsx`, so the three surfaces share one
  answer instead of three near-copies.

**No new endpoint, permission model, authoring switch or translation key.** The URL was
already in hand on every arm: `readFileValue` returns the expanded value's own `url`, or
derives the stable `/api/v1/storage/files/:id` endpoint from a bare id — and that
endpoint already 302-redirects to a freshly-signed short-lived URL per request. The link
text is the file name, which is also the anchor's accessible name, so nothing new had to
be translated; a value carrying no name of its own still falls back to the existing
`fields.file.fileFallback` key. Anchors carry `target="_blank"` plus
`rel="noopener noreferrer"` and stop click propagation, mirroring `UrlCellRenderer` and
`ImageCellRenderer`.

`video` / `audio` ride the same cell-renderer entry and therefore gain the same
affordance. That is pinned rather than left as a side effect.

## Clause-② — still `no`, re-checked against the implementation

No symbol is added to `@object-ui/fields`' published surface: `file-affordance.tsx` is
imported by two modules and deliberately NOT re-exported from the barrel.
`CellRendererProps` is untouched. No authoring shape changed — the widened *reading* is
`readFileValues`, which this package already applied to `image` and which `FileField`
already applied to `file` values.

## Behaviour that moved, deliberately

- A NON-EMPTY array no longer renders only its count. The count survives where it is the
  whole truth: an array that resolves to no renderable file still states `0 files`
  through the same i18n channel — objectui#8496's invariant and objectui#8441's channel,
  both re-pinned on that arm.
- A value that resolves to no URL renders as plain text, ⛔ never a dead anchor — the
  ruling objectui#8490 made for `email` / `url` / `phone`, applied to this family.
- ⚠️ **`file` / `video` / `audio` move into `CHIP_UNFIT_RENDERER_TYPES`
  (`packages/plugin-detail`).** The `summaryFields` chip beside the record H1 hosts text,
  not controls — objectui#8464's own stated rule, with its census asserting exactly that.
  Giving the cell renderer an anchor makes these three fail that rule, so the chip now
  draws them through `coerceToSafeValue`. Its TEXT is byte-unchanged (`coerceToSafeValue`
  reads the same `name` the renderer reads); the file stays reachable one band down, in
  the field's own cell. ⛔ The alternative — teaching the cell renderer which SURFACE it
  is drawing into — was refused: it widens published surface for a distinction neither
  card asks for.

## Pins

New: `packages/fields/src/__tests__/fileReadonlyDownload-9161.test.tsx` — 17 cases over
the cell renderer, both widget surfaces, the bare-id arm, the no-URL arm, the `rel` /
`target` contract, `video` / `audio`, and the two invariants above.

Updated (never deleted, never weakened from `toBe` to `toContain`), each carrying
objectui#9161 and the reason written at the assertion:

- `cellRenderers.countLabelI18n-8441.test.tsx` — the three `file` cases whose counts were
  taken on a NON-empty array; they now assert the new text exactly, plus the anchor's
  `href`, and re-pin objectui#8441's own subject on the `0 files` arm.
- `cellRenderers.objectLiteral-8596.test.tsx` — the real-file-array case.
- `summaryChip.badgeFitCensus-8464.test.tsx` — a fifth refusal class,
  `interactive-control`; 38/15 becomes 35/18.
- `summaryChip.objectValue-8464.test.tsx` — the `file` row moves from `RENDERER_BACKED`
  to its own refused-side case, keeping its value assertion unchanged.
- `DetailSection.copyObjectValues-8395.test.tsx` — the rendered-text CONTROL for
  `Attachments`; that file's actual subject, the clipboard payload, is untouched.

## Departure from the dispatched file surface

`packages/plugin-detail` is outside the declared surface for this card. It is reached
because `plugin-detail` consumes `getCellRenderer`, and objectui#8464's census is the
instrument that measures which kinds fit the chip — it went red exactly as designed. The
four files above are the whole extent of it.

## Verification

All readings below were taken at `b548248`, the branch head, after the final commit.

**The new pins fail before the change and pass after** — both readings from the real run
output, not from an editor exit code. RED was measured on the unmodified tree with only
the test file added, GREEN after the implementation landed:

- RED: `Test Files 1 failed (1)` · `Tests 11 failed | 6 passed (17)`, exit 1. The
  first failure is `expected null to be ...` from
  `getByRole('link', { name: 'att-1928.txt' })` — there was no anchor to find.
- GREEN: `Test Files 1 passed (1)` · `Tests 17 passed (17)`, exit 0.

One RED-run finding was folded back in: the `rel` / `target` case passed vacuously at
RED, because a `for` loop over zero anchors satisfies every assertion inside it. It now
asserts the anchor count first.

**Whole affected packages** (`pnpm exec vitest run packages/fields/ packages/plugin-detail/`
from the repo root, serialized through the shared verify lock):

- before the pin updates: `Test Files 5 failed | 334 passed (339)` · `Tests 7 failed | 4444 passed (4451)`
- after: `Test Files 339 passed (339)` · `Tests 4451 passed (4451)`, exit 0

**Consumers outside those two packages** — every test file outside them that declares a
`file`-typed field (`ActionParamDialog`, `ActionParamDialog.uploading`,
`RecordDetailView.approvalDeclaredActions`, `paramToField`, `ObjectKanban.requiredWhenPrompt`,
`deriveMasterDetail`, `view-config-utils`): `Test Files 7 passed (7)` · `Tests 152 passed (152)`.

**Build + typecheck**: the dependency closure of both packages built, then
`type-check` for `@object-ui/fields` and `@object-ui/plugin-detail` — both `Done`, exit 0.
Build is what makes the typecheck real: on an unbuilt closure every workspace import
reads as `TS2307` and the run says nothing about this diff.

**Lint**: `eslint --no-inline-config` over the 11 changed paths — exit 0, **0 errors**,
195 warnings, none of them new. The narrowing is a measurement and not a skip: the
population is eslint's own (all 11 paths were actually linted, so none is excluded by the
config's `ignores` — the `.changeset` file reports "ignored because no matching
configuration", which is the expected answer for Markdown); the file count is read from
`--format json`; and type-aware linting is NOT enabled in `eslint.config.js` (no
`parserOptions.project`, no `projectService`), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any
file it did not touch. The one `no-unused-vars` warning inside the touched region
(`isMultiple` in `FileCellRenderer`) is present on `ff1d5ea` byte for byte and is not
introduced here. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` run stays CI's.

**Gates**, all exit 0: `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:i18n-dead-keys`,
`check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`,
`check:self-import`, `check:esm-specifiers`, `check:side-effects-array`,
`check:lint-rule-coverage`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`,
`check:spec-symbols`, `check:dist-completeness`, `check:changeset-presence`,
`check:changeset-no-major`, `check:governed-queue-guard --test` (NOT GOVERNED, 11 paths
checked against 5 governed surfaces, none matched).

**NOT MEASURED locally**, each because its own prerequisite is a build this run did not
do — not because it failed: `check:readme-exports` (needs every package built; it reports
a collapsed population and says so itself), `check:eager-closure` and
`check:sdui-registration-pins` (both read `apps/console/dist`). CI builds first and
decides all three.
